A huge brute of a man entered the Credo-side building and emerged on the Star Town side — a crossing that is not supposed to be possible. This implies a connection or passage through the fence between the two buildings
Kostas and StClair scoped out the security system. It looks unsophisticated; the crew believe they could shut down the alarms if they decide to break in
Ozy successfully hacked Winter Shipping’s systems remotely, but found almost nothing of interest — suspiciously little. The crew suspect the real records sit on a separate, unconnected system
The Star Town side operates a launch that runs up to Regina Highport
Ozy found flight records showing that some of those launch runs take hours longer than the trip should
The crew decided against breaking in for now. Plan: cross into Star Town, walk into the Winter Shipping offices with a legitimate piece of business as cover, and see what they can learn face to face
Kostas Backett bought a dagger in Star Town for protection. Regina is Law Level 9, where all weapons are banned — carrying it is illegal anywhere on the moon. The crew judge Star Town lawless enough to carry it there, and Kostas intends to drop it before returning to Credo City
Inside, the Star Town Winter Shipping office is very fancy — far smarter than the surroundings suggest. Behind the desk is Marid, a very attractive receptionist
The legitimate business used as cover was the crew’s cargo from Yori: 3 tons of crystals and gems, bought for Cr54,000 and sold for Cr72,000 — a Cr18,000 profit. That is the Event Horizon’s entire 3-ton hold
The sale is to Winter Shipping itself. Olso, the crew’s Winter Shipping contact, will be picking the cargo up — giving the crew a legitimate reason to observe Winter Shipping personnel and their collection process
Admiral Cassius called Pallod Norrim to try to find out what happened to the surviving Dancado intruder taken into POC custody
Pallod Norrim is no longer taking the crew’s calls. Nothing was learned about the prisoner
The crew set off for the 10pm meeting with Detective Odoy at The Flotsam
Detective Odoy tells the crew he is investigating Ven Yasha, and that he believes Ven Yasha killed Vlen Backett — directly contradicting Pallod Norrim’s official line that Darrian Jak is the murderer. Odoy’s claim is unverified
Odoy’s theory is that Vlen was working as a courier for Ven Yasha. Unverified, but it would fit Vlen’s constant travel and improbable contacts
Further from Odoy (all his account, unverified):

No Zhodani spy was killed. The murder behind the rumour is Vlen, and he was not a spy — the spy story is a cover used to justify the Imperial police takeover of the inquiry
Imperial security have been everywhere on Regina
The Imperial force that arrived aboard the Alahir are after Ven Yasha
Odoy knows little about Iaros Ujinka or why she would be killed
The Dancado prisoner is no longer in POC custody — and the Imperial force also collected the other man from that attack
The red-haired man appears to be a fixer called Harlen, who is connected to Winter Shipping


Open question: Pallod Norrim named the short redhead as Darrian Jak and arrested him; Odoy names the red-haired man as Harlen. Whether Jak and Harlen are the same person, two different redheads, or an alias is not established

Decisions and discoveries

Winter Shipping occupies two buildings straddling the Credo City/Star Town fence, with an apparent internal passage between them — a man was seen entering one side and emerging on the other
The Credo-side office is closed and redirects callers to Star Town. Security on the premises is unsophisticated and the crew believe they could defeat the alarms
Winter Shipping’s networked systems hold almost nothing. The crew infer a second, unconnected system holding the real records — an inference, not confirmed
Winter Shipping runs a launch from the Star Town side to Regina Highport, and some of those runs take hours longer than the journey should. Unexplained
The crew sold their Yori cargo — 3 tons of crystals and gems — to Winter Shipping for Cr72,000 against a Cr54,000 outlay, using the sale as cover and a way to observe the company. Olso is the contact collecting it
Pallod Norrim has stopped taking the crew’s calls entirely. Nothing was learned about the Dancado prisoner through him
Detective Odoy gave a wholly different account of the case from Pallod’s. Everything below is Odoy’s claim and none of it is independently verified:

Ven Yasha, not Darrian Jak, killed Vlen Backett
Vlen was a courier for Ven Yasha
The Zhodani spy story is false. The murder it refers to is Vlen’s, and the spy framing exists to justify the Imperial police takeover of the inquiry
The Imperial force aboard the Alahir is hunting Ven Yasha, and Imperial security are all over Regina
Both Dancado attackers — the dead man and the prisoner — have been taken by that Imperial force. The prisoner is no longer in POC custody
The red-haired man is a fixer named Harlen, connected to Winter Shipping
Odoy has no explanation for Iaros Ujinka’s murder


Two independent sources now attach Ven Yasha to the case: the Dancado prisoner named him under questioning, and Odoy’s whole investigation is built on him
Unresolved identity: Pallod’s arrested suspect Darrian Jak and Odoy’s fixer Harlen are both short red-haired men tied to this murder. Whether they are the same man, an alias, or two people is not established
Harlen’s link to Winter Shipping ties the crew’s own recon to Odoy’s account: the same company took Vlen’s last call, employs a fixer matching the third man, and runs unexplained flights to the Highport
Odoy’s own agency, motives and reason for approaching the crew remain unrecorded

End position

The crew are at The Flotsam on the night of 195-1105, having just heard out Detective Odoy
The POC’s official case (Jak did it, case closed) and Odoy’s account (Yasha did it, the Imperials are hunting Yasha, the spy story is a cover) are in direct conflict. The crew have no way yet to test either
Pallod Norrim is unreachable; both Dancado attackers are beyond the crew’s reach in Imperial hands
Winter Shipping is now the strongest live lead: Vlen’s last call, Harlen’s employer, an internal fence crossing, a soft alarm system and unexplained Highport launches
The crew are up Cr18,000 on the Yori cargo, with the Event Horizon’s 3-ton hold empty pending collection by Olso
Kostas Backett remains injured at STR 3, DEX 9, END 1
Iaros Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research is still unanswered

Priorities for next session

Break into Winter Shipping — the alarms look beatable; the targets are the second, unnetworked system, the passage between the two buildings, and anything on the Highport launch runs
Find out more about the Alahir — its captain, its crew, and the Imperial force Odoy says it carries
Try to meet Darrian Jak in prison — test Pallod’s case and settle whether Jak is Harlen

session-2026-08-23.title: Session 2026-08-23
session-2026-08-23.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-08-23
In-fiction date: 195-1105, evening, running into the early hours of 196-1105
Starting position
The crew are at The Flotsam late on 195-1105, having just heard out Detective Odoy.

Two irreconcilable accounts of Vlen Backett’s Murder are on the table: the POC’s (Darrian Jak did it, closed) and Odoy’s (Ven Yasha did it, Vlen was his courier, the Imperials are here for Yasha). Neither verified
Pallod Norrim is unreachable; both Dancado attackers are in Imperial hands
Winter Shipping is the strongest lead: Vlen’s last call, Harlen’s employer, two buildings straddling the Credo City/Star Town fence, soft alarms, a near-empty network and launch runs to Regina Highport that take hours too long
The crew are Cr18,000 up on the Yori cargo, sold to Winter Shipping as cover; Olso is collecting it
Kostas Backett remains injured at STR 3, DEX 9, END 1

Live notes

Planning discussion first. Options weighed: break into Winter Shipping, visit Darrian Jak in prison, investigate the Alahir. The break-in won
The Event Horizon, in orbit around Assiniboia, can track Winter Shipping’s launch once it lifts. There is only one launch, parked by the Star Town office. Tracking alone is impractical without knowing which run is the anomalous one — hence the need for the flight schedule
Rejected as unworkable: astrogation to narrow down destinations from flight durations, faking shipping documents (nobody has Streetwise), buying or building tracking drones, and shipping Kostas up in a crate
The crew have no weapons — Regina is Law Level 9. StClair has a plastic knife
They approached the closed Credo-side office after dark. The group stealth check failed — the party were seen loitering and their presence noted as suspicious. They withdrew and tried again
Long tangent on distractions (faking a heart attack for the Admiral, StClair stabbing him in the leg, a bomb in a bin). None used
Kostas went in alone and aced it. He reached the building unseen, disabled the alarms on an electronics/sensors roll, slipped inside and opened a side access for the others
Inside the Credo-side building: dark, mostly empty crate tables — and one room in the far corner with a door ajar, light, muttering and the tapping of data pads
Through the door: a hermetically sealed environmental chamber with a Llellewyoly — a “Dandelion” — inside, working an enormous volume of data across multiple pads and monitors on a closed system. This is why the hacked server held nothing
Below the floor the crew found a ramp down into a tunnel running towards the Star Town building. Not concealed. Down the tunnel: a newer pipe with vents at equal intervals (unexplained), and a storeroom holding empty gin bottles and crates of non-human food. StClair ate some and vomited. The far end has a ramp up on the Star Town side, closed, with no mechanism visible from the tunnel
Long argument over killing it, kidnapping it, poisoning its food or hacking it. An electronics check confirmed no external route into its system — kidnap or conversation only. The crew chose to talk
Ozy and Cassius knocked on the glass. It answered on a comm unit: “I am exceedingly discreet. What is your title at this time, strangers?” — recorded as Exceedingly Discreet. It addresses everyone by invented titles: “overly dressed pompous man” (Cassius), “pale-skinned smartly dressed man” (Ozy), “downtrodden depressed man” (Kostas), “unruly-haired rude scientist man” (StClair, after he greeted it as a “ballsack with chicken legs”)
Cassius’ cover story — an external security audit — was dismissed as illogical, as was a follow-up about missing cargo. The crew then told it the truth: Vlen’s murder, Iaros Ujinka’s murder, the TAS footage, the man present at both killings, the POC-liveried grav car, The Device, and that they are looking for Harlen and for Ven Yasha
It took the truth well. It is the brains of the operation, and says Harlen runs the company — “short-sighted and a poor tactician”, but loyal. Ven Yasha hired them all. It thinks Harlen is not the right person to be running Winter Shipping long-term, and that the crew’s evidence marks him as a failure
The deal, agreed: it puts the crew on Winter Shipping’s launch and up to the company’s station in orbit, where Harlen is. In return the crew guarantee Harlen does not survive, and never report the conversation. Its own ambition — taking over the company — is the crew’s guarantee it won’t turn them in
It can control the launch’s flight path from its terminal. Marid does not need to know. It suggests the launch rendezvous with the Event Horizon in orbit so the crew can arm themselves — they will have to deal with the station’s staff and Harlen, and Credo weapons law makes arming on the ground impossible
What it gave up, all its own account and unverified:

Ven Yasha ordered Iaros Ujinka’s death. It does not understand why, and says so plainly — greater understanding of Ancient technology would only raise the value of Ancient artefacts
Vlen Backett was a messenger for Ven Yasha — “he must have brought bad news, hence his demise”
It was aware of both murders
On what Yasha wants from Ancient technology: nobody understands the secrets of the Ancients, but the potential runs to immortality, taking systems, taking the Imperium, destroying armies. It knows of no specific plan
Harlen holds some of Vlen’s possessions — a statuette, and data crystals. Volunteered unprompted, because Kostas is his nephew
Imperial Intelligence were on Regina in numbers. They arrived on the Alahir, which has since departed — whatever their business was, it is concluded. The captain’s name was heard as “Gand Hulses” (spelling unconfirmed) and he is said to hold some special portfolio in the intelligence services. It does not know whether they came for Yasha or for something else
It refuses to discuss Ven Yasha himself at all — “for my own survival” — while offering information on Harlen, on the hired thugs, and on Imperial Intelligence
On Harlen’s weaknesses: none as such. Loyal to Yasha and not for turning. “He is just a man, though”


Session ended in the small hours of 196-1105, in the Credo-side office, deal struck

Decisions and discoveries

Winter Shipping’s real records live in a Llellewyoly’s head and on a closed system in the Credo-side office. The empty server is explained
Exceedingly Discreet — the Llellewyoly — is now an ally of convenience with its own agenda: it wants Harlen dead and the company for itself
Harlen runs Winter Shipping, and Ven Yasha hired all of them. First confirmation from inside the company of the Yasha link that Detective Odoy alleged
Ven Yasha ordered Iaros Ujinka’s murder (per Exceedingly Discreet). The motive is unexplained even to the company’s own brain
Vlen Backett was Yasha’s messenger — a second, independent version of Odoy’s courier claim
Harlen holds Vlen’s statuette and data crystals — the first concrete object of Vlen’s known to be in the killers’ hands
There is a Winter Shipping station in orbit — the destination of the overlong launch runs, and where Harlen is
The Alahir has left Regina, its Imperial Intelligence contingent’s business concluded. Its captain reportedly holds a special intelligence portfolio; name heard as “Gand Hulses”, spelling and identity unconfirmed
The tunnel between the two buildings is real and unconcealed, with a closed ramp at the Star Town end and an unexplained newer, vented pipe running its length
The party still have no weapons and no Streetwise; almost every plan this session failed on a missing skill
The crew have promised to kill Harlen. Nobody has yet raised what happens if that turns out to be a lie told to them by a plant

End position

Early hours of 196-1105, inside the closed Credo-side Winter Shipping office, with the deal struck and Exceedingly Discreet still at its console
The route up is arranged: Winter Shipping’s launch, its flight path set by Exceedingly Discreet, with a rendezvous with the Event Horizon in orbit to collect weapons before boarding the station
Marid, Olso and the rest of the company are unaware of any of it
Kostas Backett is still at STR 3, DEX 9, END 1. StClair has been sick and has a plastic knife
Iaros Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research is still unanswered

Priorities for next session

Arm the crew — rendezvous with the Event Horizon in orbit and get real weapons aboard before the station
Take the launch to the Winter Shipping Station — deal with the staff, find Harlen
Recover Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals from Harlen
Decide how far to honour the deal — the crew have promised a killing, and Exceedingly Discreet keeps its own counsel about Ven Yasha

session-2026-09-06.title: Session 2026-09-06
session-2026-09-06.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-09-06
In-fiction date: 196-1105, from the small hours through to the morning
Starting position
The crew are inside Winter Shipping’s closed Credo-side office in the small hours of 196-1105, deal struck with Exceedingly Discreet: passage up to the company’s orbital base in exchange for Harlen’s death.

The route up is arranged — the company launch, flight path set from Exceedingly Discreet’s console, Marid unaware
The crew have no weapons; Regina is Law Level 9
Kostas Backett is badly injured at STR 3, DEX 9, END 1
Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals are said to be in Harlen’s hands, aboard the base

Live notes

StClair sat the raid out. He went back to the Event Horizon in a mood to do research, leaving the two least effective combat characters to board a hostile installation. He handed Kostas a medikit on the way out
The Implacable had already returned to the Event Horizon — its mooring fees at Regina Highport were only paid so far. It met the launch in orbit as planned and the crew armed there
Backup: Gunner Gunnerson, the Event Horizon’s gunner — a grizzled ex-Marine in a filthy boiler suit, chewing a cigar, rolled up as elite. Announced himself with “did someone call for backup?” Run by Kostas’ player as a second character. Stealth −4; he does not sneak
The base is not a station. The launch flew out to a semi-stable Lagrangian point between Regina and Assiniboia, into a container yard — thousands of cargo containers docked into long lines and cubes, some drifting free and untethered, nav buoys and warning beacons among them. The launch dipped beneath a trio of old containers, a concealed hatch opened, and it docked inside
Interior: three shipping containers bolted together. No lights anywhere — the staff know their way around in the dark. Doors barely airtight, everything cobbled together. The dock bay held only the launch and a few sealed crates
First firefight — the dock level. Gunnerson took point, opened the door and got a surprise round on a man standing with his back turned, mid-conversation with someone in the toilet

Gunnerson’s opening shot tore into his back for 19 and left him at END 0, still standing
Kostas fired Vlen’s gun for 9 once the laser sight and P-HUD bonuses were found — the table spent a while working out that the sheet wasn’t including them
Ozy leaned through the doorway at −1 and hit the ceiling
Cassius rolled Leadership for Effect 5 — five DM+1 tokens to hand out over the fight, and they carried most of the party’s hits
Gunnerson aimed and finished him for 35 damage, at which point the GM retconned his laser rifle down to a carbine for being wildly overpowered. Reduced to 27; the man’s top half was obliterated
The second man burst out of the toilet still pulling his trousers up. Kostas shot him for 15 — “this one’s for the Admiral” — the Effect wiping out his protection entirely. He was flung back into the toilet, dropped his gun and slipped in the mess. Cassius finished him with the machine gun
The bodies yielded a stub pistol and some cigarettes. Nothing else


The machine gun was loud. Movement was heard on the floor above, reached by an airlock and ladder
Second firefight — the upper level. A long cover fight against the base’s smugglers, most shots hitting cover rather than people. Gunnerson went up first, called down that he could see two or three, and fought from cover the whole way

Ozy missed repeatedly, then discovered his damage dice were configured wrong on Roll20 — rolling a flat +3 instead of 3D6. Corrected mid-fight
One smuggler charged out, slipped on his mate’s corpse and went prone at −6. Kostas gut-shot him dead
Cassius came up, dropped one with the Gauss rifle for 9 through no cover, and another later with a body shot
Kostas was shot for 3 through his flak jacket (Protection 5) — enough to take END to 0 and put him on STR. He was hit again shortly after


Kostas’ self-treatment failed. With no doctor in reach, he used StClair’s medikit (TL10, DM+1) on himself and rolled Effect −4. The GM checked the rules, found nothing that defines the consequence of a failed first aid, and homeruled it: no characteristics regained, no further damage — “killing yourself with a third medic roll is insane” — and the medikit is spent. StClair owes himself a new one
Gunnerson later broke off to bandage Kostas for 1 point, taken on END
Harlen appeared. A red-haired man, arriving late into the fight. He shot at Gunnerson and missed, then began shouting to rally his people

Then he saw Kostas — and his expression changed. He muttered “oh”. He looked across at the Admiral’s uniform, said “This is suboptimal”, and closed his eyes
Every screen in the base went black. An alarm sounded and a synthesised voice announced: destruct sequence activated, detonation imminent, all hands to re-entry capsules. Floor lights lit a path of white arrows to an airlock, which popped open
Thirty seconds to detonation. Harlen simply stood there with his eyes closed


The crew debated staying to grab something versus running. Cassius made the executive decision to go. Kostas wanted Harlen taken alive — “shoot him in the legs, Gunner” — reasoning he wouldn’t blow a station he was still standing on. Harlen legged it before anyone could act on it
The launch was never an escape route. It was on an automated flight path controlled remotely by Exceedingly Discreet, and had already detached. The only way off was the escape capsules
Down at the capsule deck the surviving smugglers were trying the hatches; the first two were locked and jammed. Kostas ran past them and a capsule lit green and opened — big enough for five. He held it and waved his gun at anyone approaching
Ozy went door-to-door on the way out. One door opened onto what looked like the base’s gun emplacement. The next opened onto Harlen at his desk — eyes closed, fingers steepled, muttering “this is not the end” over and over

On the desk: a statuette Ozy recognised as the same sort of thing that was in Professor Ujinka’s house, and a set of data disks
He grabbed both and ran. He did not touch Harlen


Gunnerson killed a smuggler at the capsules and took a parting shot at the last one as the capsule launched. The crew left the final smuggler alive, still trying to force a jammed hatch
The base died about twenty seconds out — imploded, scrunched up, then blew outward. The capsule rode the edge of the wave, guided itself down, and landed in wild land on the outskirts of the Twin Cities on Regina. Grav bikes were waiting at what looked like a designated recovery point
GM: “You’ve completed Chapter 1.”

Decisions and discoveries

Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals are recovered — the party’s stated objective for the raid, achieved in the last thirty seconds of it. Presumed Vlen’s on strong circumstantial grounds; nobody in the fiction confirmed it
The statuette resembles Iaros Ujinka’s Ancient material. The first physical object linking Vlen, Ujinka’s Research and Ven Yasha’s organisation
The “station” was a hidden base — three containers bolted together, buried in a Lagrangian container yard, unlit and unregistered. It is destroyed.
Harlen triggered the self-destruct by closing his eyes. Screens blacked out and the station obeyed him with no console, no keypad and no spoken command. Psionics, an implant, or something else is not established — but the GM flagged his red hair repeatedly and gave him “this is not the end” as an exit line
Harlen recognised Kostas on sight, and recognised Cassius’ uniform. He knew who they were before they said a word
Harlen’s fate is unknown. He was last seen at his desk as the countdown ran, and the base was destroyed. Nobody saw him board a capsule and nobody saw him die. The promise to Exceedingly Discreet is fulfilled only by assumption
Gunner Gunnerson carried the fight. Both firefights turned on his shooting, and he twice broke off to drag or patch Kostas
The failed medic check is now settled as a house rule: no gain, no extra harm, equipment consumed

End position

Morning of 196-1105, standing in wild land outside the Twin Cities on Regina with grav bikes available and a ride back into the city
Kostas Backett at roughly STR 1, DEX 2, END 1 — three damaged characteristics, needs surgery, and cannot heal on rest. The Event Horizon’s sickbay is the fix
The party hold a statuette and data disks neither of them has examined
Winter Shipping’s orbital base, its records of whatever moved through it, and most of its staff are gone. Exceedingly Discreet is still at its console in Credo, and does not yet know
Iaros Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research is still unanswered

Priorities for next session

Get Kostas into surgery — the ship’s sickbay, or a Regina hospital
Examine the statuette and the data disks — the first material from Vlen’s own hands
Establish whether Harlen is dead, and what he actually was
Face Exceedingly Discreet — its company just exploded, and the crew were the last people aboard
Still open and deprioritised: Darrian Jak in prison, Detective Odoy’s motives, The Device

session-2026-09-13.title: Session 2026-09-13
session-2026-09-13.content:
traveller sota session
Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-09-13
In-fiction date: 196-1105, morning — then two or three days into jump
GM’s framing: an in-between-chapters session — take on passengers for the next trip, tidy loose ends, then downtime in jump for training. Delivered as promised: trade and passenger rolls, a surgery, a lore drop, and a jump. “A bit bitty, but you’re on your way.”
Starting position
Morning of 196-1105, in wild land outside the Twin Cities on Regina with grav bikes and a ride back into the city. Chapter 1 complete; the base is destroyed.

Kostas Backett at STR 1 · DEX 2 · END 1 — needs surgery (failed surgery costs 3 + Effect more; at STR 1 that’s lethal). Ship’s sickbay or a Regina hospital
Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals in hand, unexamined
Harlen’s fate unknown — “this is not the end”
Exceedingly Discreet does not yet know its base is gone
Iaros Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research still unanswered
StClair’s medikit is spent
Vlen’s body and estate still with the POC; Kostas is next of kin

Prep notes

Get Kostas to a hospital, he needs surgery (medic check, p.82)

Ask about Slow Drug
Get END to 7 (max), then…
Medical care on the ship: 3 + END DM (0) + doctor’s medical skill per day
5 days max to get back to normal


Examine the statuette, read the data disks
Decide where we’re going, get trade and passengers

Careful with the passengers, we’ve caused a bit of trouble on Regina


Confront Exceedingly Discreet - what wasn’t he telling us about Harlen?
Where is Vlen’s body right now? I should probably do something with that
Training in downtime

x8 weeks of 8hrs/day
EDU check (8+)



Live notes

Split up at the landing site. The crew were still carrying weapons they’re not allowed to hold on Law Level 9 Regina, and Kostas was bleeding out. Gunnerson took Kostas straight back up to the Event Horizon along with the statuette and the data disks; Cassius and Ozy went back into Credo to tie up loose ends. Cover story if asked: they’d gone exploring outside the city and been ambushed. Cassius offered up his own savings to cover whatever the trip needed
Kostas suggested from his sickbed that the others find Detective Odoy and give him an update — “let him keep causing more trouble for Ven Yasha”. It didn’t happen. GM: “Detective Odoy will never know what happened. He probably wouldn’t believe you anyway”
Winter Shipping’s Credo office — a dead end. Cassius and Ozy went back in. Exceedingly Discreet was gone — “the daffodil guy” is no longer in its sealed chamber, and nothing in the building indicated where it went. Ozy’s one good Recon roll of the campaign turned up a receipt for the trade the crew did with Winter Shipping earlier — something they already knew about — and nothing else; the computers gave nothing. They were making the neighbours suspicious, so they left on a cover story about a package in transit being with a different courier. Ideas about checking shipping/taxi companies or finding where Dandelions congregate were floated and dropped: “this feels like a dead end”. Back up to the Highport on the hourly shuttle
Destination: Alell — Vlen’s homeworld and the Backetts’, and where his body is to be buried. The GM noted Kostas is from Roup and that Ozy’s homeworld is Uakye, “right next door to Alell”
Route. The Event Horizon is Jump-2, so Alell is three jumps minimum, about three weeks: Regina → Forboldn (two parsecs) → Whanga → Alell. Passengers could be sought for three destinations at two, four and five parsecs. Cassius asked for a pit stop at Barbag; the GM confirmed these are the real map names, not made up to sound rude
Passengers. The ship’s steward, Talia (Steward 3), rolled for high passage to Alell: Steward +3, high passage −4, starport A +5 (heard as), population/destination modifiers, came out at 11 people wanting high passage to Alell. Cassius’s idea of auctioning tickets to the highest bidder was withdrawn when the GM said a bad Streetwise roll would lose passengers. GM first ruled double occupancy for ten, then re-read the rule: high passage is one per stateroom, so five. Middle passage the same, basic passage two to a room. Five high passengers to Alell at Cr60,000 each = Cr300,000 if they arrive safely

Vetting. Nobody has Investigate. Cassius rolled Streetwise and the table declared the passengers “fantastic people… so on the level you don’t even need a spirit level” while describing them as Jeffrey Dahmer and Fred West lookalikes. The GM then rolled on a D66 table for each of the five, privately: “Now I know who your high passengers are. And you guys don’t.” Gunnerson looked them over and called the crew stupid. Kostas was in the medbay and saw none of it
Passengers can roam the ship but not the research labs or delicate areas
Each high passenger uses a ton of cargo space; the ship has 12 tons. Low passage was considered but the Event Horizon has no low berths


Cargo. Ozy (Broker 1) rolled for incidental cargo: 15 lots available, two rolled at 6 tons and 4 tons. The 6-ton lot was advanced electronics, base Cr100,000; the supplier wanted 110% and Ozy’s broker roll couldn’t beat it. Declined — and by refusing, the crew have burned their bridges with Regina’s legal suppliers for a month. GM hinted at other, less legal suppliers; the crew voted passengers over cargo instead
Finances. Kostas’s spreadsheet first said Cr236,000 a month in costs and Cr148,000 short; he then found a subtotal error — the ship was actually only Cr33,500 short for the month before this trip, having made Cr70,000 from passengers to Regina and Cr18,000 on the Regina cargo. The month falls due after two jumps; with Cr300,000 in passage fees the ship is in the black. GM: “You can’t pay late. Well, you can — you’ll just have people after you”
Fuel. The lab ship sat skimming Assiniboia while the crew were on Regina. No roll is needed to skim, only to do it faster; Forboldn and Whanga both have gas giants, so the route can be flown on free fuel
Crew pay. A Perception check (an easy 6) showed Talia was pissed off at five passengers landing on her while paid Cr2,000 a month — “Talia the underpaid”. Ozy knew the figure. The crew doubled her to Cr4,000; she went “from not trusting you to mildly suspicious”. Gunnerson is on Cr4,000 and the crew talked about a performance bonus for keeping them alive — undecided. The second gunner, Atticus Brown, is cheap: he just wanted off-planet. Crew wages now Cr9,000 a month from Cr7,000
Kostas’s surgery. Done in the Event Horizon’s medbay (DM+1, treats up to five patients) by StClair, Medic 2, total DM+3, “up to his ass in research” and still mourning Ujinka. Succeeded — END up from 1 to 5. Kostas plans the daily medical care from there: END to 7 and DEX up on day one, DEX to full on day two, STR sorted two days after. Two days of healing already banked by session end
The lore drop. The GM shared three of Ujinka’s research notes, recovered by Ozy from her computer at Dancado — see that note for the text — and described the statuette and disks:

The statuette is a winged pillar of an ivory-like substance. Scanned with the ship’s sensors: a work of art, not a technological device. All evidence points to it being of Ancients origin
It is the statue from Research Note 2 — the one a trader pulled from the asteroid belt in the Boughene system, which Ujinka’s margin note says Vlen asked to borrow “for analysis by one of his contacts”. Vlen somehow got hold of it; the disks corroborate the match
The disks cover the Boughene asteroid belt and the g-band fluctuations described in Note 2, and include a note from Vlen reminding himself to acquire the Professor’s g-band sensor system and use it to scan the Boughene system
Note 1 is about the g-band “dead zone” method, and names Juni — StClair’s ex-wife — as taking the work to the Ancients site on Beck’s World. StClair reacted to her name
GM’s plain-English gloss: unnatural interference on a band nobody at the table understands, which Ujinka — and Vlen — thought was a way to track down remaining Ancient sites, “and maybe the secrets of the Ancients”


The Event Horizon is in one piece: the two research companies aboard, Helix and Black Horizon, “haven’t killed each other”, and Talia reported a quiet few days. Gunnerson is regaling anyone who’ll listen about his deeds on the base — his shin is still sore from where the Admiral kicked him, though it did shake an extra clip of ammo out of his pocket
Jump to Forboldn. Cassius ran the ship computer: astrogation succeeded with Effect +1, jump drive roll came up +6. “Off to hell!” — 7 days 5 hours in jump. D100 for random encounters came up clear
Downtime. Cassius is training — Investigate was the joke, “some fucking thing we haven’t got” — and needs eight weeks of it. StClair is researching; the GM hinted something might come of it. Using a skill at the table does not count towards training it
Cliffhanger, second or third morning in jump. Talia came onto the bridge with a stern face: “I’m going to need your help on something.” A discovery has been made combining Helix equipment with Black Horizon research, and the two teams are in a blazing row over who owns it — patents, royalties, ownership. The passengers haven’t caught wind yet. Ozy intends to settle it with Advocate — he claims the charter contract has a clause defaulting disputed joint discoveries to the carrier, i.e. the ship; GM: “good try, we’ll see”. A well-thought-out approach may earn a Boon. Parked for next session

Decisions and discoveries

The ship is bound for Alell, three jumps out, carrying five high passengers of unknown character. Vlen’s home, his family, and his burial. Route Forboldn → Whanga → Alell; first leg under way
Exceedingly Discreet has gone. No trace at the Credo office. It knows its base is gone or it doesn’t; either way it’s no longer where the crew can reach it. The Winter Shipping thread on Regina is closed for now
Detective Odoy was not told anything. The crew left Regina without reporting back to anyone
The statuette is Ancient, is art, and came from Boughene’s asteroid belt — the trader’s find in Ujinka’s Note 2, which Vlen “borrowed”. It’s a fragment of what Ujinka called a larger anchor array. This is the first physical link between Vlen, Ujinka’s g-band work and a specific system
Vlen intended to scan Boughene with Ujinka’s g-band sensor system — the disks say so in his own words. His funding-and-a-ship offer had a target
Ujinka’s Research now has text. Three notes: the g-band dead-zone method (Note 1), the Boughene log and the statue (Note 2), and the Deneb conference claim that the Ancients were a single unified entity that “engineered the very matter to resist time” (Note 3)
StClair’s ex-wife is Juni, and she is working the Ancients site on Beck’s World right now
Regina’s legal cargo suppliers are closed to the crew for a month
Kostas is out of danger — surgery succeeded, END 5 and climbing
Rules settled at the table: high/middle passage is one passenger per stateroom; each high passenger consumes a ton of cargo space; skimming needs no roll; a failed surgery costs 3 + Effect (confirmed from p.82 but not tested); skill use doesn’t count as training

End position

Two or three days into a 7-day jump from Regina to Forboldn, first of three legs to Alell
Five high passengers aboard, vetted by vibes; the GM knows who they are
A patent row between Helix and Black Horizon is boiling on the lab decks; Talia has asked the crew to intervene
Kostas Backett at END 5, DEX and STR still damaged, on daily medical care from StClair; expected back to full within about four days
Cassius two days into eight weeks of training
Cr300,000 due on arrival at Alell; the month’s Cr33,500 shortfall is covered by it. Crew wages Cr9,000
Harlen still unaccounted for. Exceedingly Discreet vanished. Detective Odoy uninformed. Vlen’s body still on Regina with the POC — the crew left without it
Ujinka’s Research: still no formal answer to her request, but the ship is carrying her notes, her statue, and Vlen’s plan to scan Boughene

Priorities for next session

Settle the Helix / Black Horizon dispute — Ozy’s Advocate roll, with the carrier clause as his line; think out the approach for a Boon
Watch the passengers — five strangers rolled on a D66 table, and the GM was pleased with the results
Finish Kostas’s recovery — daily medical care until STR/DEX/END are back to 7/10/7
Cassius’s training, eight weeks of it; StClair’s research
Read the rest of the disks — only the Boughene material and Vlen’s reminder have been described so far
Decide what the ship does about Boughene — Vlen’s intended scan target — and about Juni on Beck’s World
Still open, further away now: Harlen, Exceedingly Discreet, Darrian Jak in prison, Detective Odoy, The Device, Vlen’s body

smashed-comms.title: Smashed Comms
smashed-comms.content:
traveller sota item clue
Secrets of the Ancients
A smashed comms unit recovered from Vlen Backett’s room at the Regina Down TAS Hostel — the room the Three Men at Vlen’s Room walked into.
Whether it was smashed by hand or knocked out by The Device is unestablished. Either way, someone did not want its contents read.
Ozy made several repair attempts. Immediately before the unit became fully damaged and unusable, he recovered the last number called: it belongs to Winter Shipping, a logistics and cargo-buying company operating in Credo City and Star Town.
Notes

solomani-hypothesis.title: Solomani Hypothesis
solomani-hypothesis.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
The theory that Humaniti originally evolved on the planet of Terra, home of the Solomani. According to it, The Ancients transplanted primitive humans to other worlds across the galaxy — most notably the homeworlds of the Vilani and the Zhodani.
Genetic evidence has largely confirmed it, though some scientists and religious groups advocate other origins for Humaniti, such as parallel evolution or divine intervention.
Why it’s in the file
Its confirmation is what gave rise to the Brotherhood of Humaniti — and the Brotherhood’s doctrine goes further, holding that the Ancients destroyed an ur-race of ‘true Humaniti’ when they split the species into tribes.
So the Ancients didn’t merely leave ruins in the Spinward Marches. They made the people currently arguing over those ruins.
Notes

spinward-marches.title: Spinward Marches
spinward-marches.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
Sector containing the Regina subsector, and within it Alell.
Ancients sites are especially common here — see The Ancients. The party are in the sector where the thing two people have been murdered over is buried.
Notes

startown.title: Startown
startown.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
The region around the old Regina starport, now the primary downport. A strip of bars, cheap hostelries, raucous entertainments and less savoury businesses — notoriously violent, corrupt and profitable.
Technically divided between the nearby cities of Credo and Atora; both blame the other for the state of it.
It is a thin strip between Credo and Atora. Winter Shipping operates here as well as in Credo City.
Regina Highport sits in geostationary orbit above Startown.
If The Flotsam is anywhere, this is the sort of district it would be in — unconfirmed.
Notes

talia.title: Talia
talia.content:
traveller sota npc
Secrets of the Ancients
Steward of the Event Horizon, Steward 3 — “one of the better stewards you’ll ever get”. Known aboard as “Talia the underpaid”: on Cr2,000 a month until 196-1105, when five high passengers landed on her and a Perception check made it obvious she was pissed off. The crew doubled her pay to Cr4,000; she went “from not trusting you to mildly suspicious”.
Runs the ship’s day-to-day while the crew are away — reported a quiet few days over the Regina stop. Two or three days into the jump to Forboldn she came onto the bridge to ask for help with the Helix / Black Horizon ownership row.
Name heard as Talia / Talley; spelling unconfirmed.
Notes

the-ancients.title: The Ancients
the-ancients.content:
traveller sota species clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Colloquial name for a species that lived 300,000 years ago. Comparatively little is known about them.
What they did

Believed responsible for transplanting Humaniti from its original homeworld of Terra (the Solomani Hypothesis) and scattering the species across hundreds of planets
Believed to have uplifted the Vargr from Terran canines
Exceedingly high technology — many artefacts are millennia beyond cutting-edge Imperial science. Estimates of high-end Ancients tech place them beyond TL25

Their sites
Several have been discovered across Charted Space, especially in the Spinward Marches — where the party currently are.

The technology at these sites varies considerably, suggesting different Ancients groups pursued radically different paths of development
Most sites show damage consistent with orbital bombardment or other violence
There are anomalies in other systems explicable only by weapons that destroyed entire planets
That, plus their sudden disappearance from known space, has produced the Ancients Extinction Theories
Ancients sites also show common use of Droyne as pets or servants

Why this matters here
Iaros Ujinka was tracing links between G-Band Transmissions and Ancients sites — see Ujinka’s Research. Vlen Backett was going to fund and crew the expedition. Both are now dead.
Threads worth holding together, none of them established:

Vlen was a man that Vargr crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult — and the Vargr are an Ancients-uplifted species
The Church of the Chosen Ones holds that Vargr are the rightful heirs of the Ancients
The Brotherhood of Humaniti holds that the Ancients broke humanity, and that institutions opposing its reunification must be destroyed
Vlen Backett’s True Age: at least 180 years old, physiologically 52, no anagathics. Nobody has explained that

Notes

the-device.title: The Device
the-device.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
The third of the Three Men at Vlen’s Room — the red-haired one whose face was never caught — carried a device that appears to have caused electrical problems.
Recorded on the board with a question mark: the connection between the device and the interference is the party’s reading of the footage, not an established fact.
“What is this device that was used?” is one of the party’s active questions. It may also explain the Smashed Comms.
Possible second sighting
At Dancado, during the attack on Iaros Ujinka, the power was cut and a security drone taken out. Electrical systems failing at the exact moment of an attack — the same signature as the interference on the hostel footage.
If that’s the same device, the same crew is running both hits, and knocking out power and security is the opening move rather than a side effect.
Kostas Backett asked Pallod Norrim about the attackers’ apparent ability to disable systems in a localised area. Pallod dismissed it, the grav car and any connection between the murders as coincidence and nothing to worry about.
Notes

the-flotsam.title: The Flotsam
the-flotsam.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
A bar. Where Detective Odoy wants to meet the party at 10pm on 195-1105 — see Meeting at the Flotsam.
The crew intend to investigate Winter Shipping first, then attend the meeting as arranged.
Notes

three-men-at-vlen's-room.title: Three Men at Vlen's Room
three-men-at-vlen's-room.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Travellers’ Aid Society security camera footage from the Regina Down TAS Hostel — obtained and viewed by the party — shows three men going to Vlen Backett’s room.

Two are on camera. Heavy-set men, dark jackets. Neither identified.
The third’s face wasn’t seen, but he had red hair.
The third man was carrying a device — see The Device.

The two on the board are shown with question marks: the party has faces, not names.
Two identified at Dancado
At Dancado, two men came in through the front door and upstairs; one was killed and the other knocked unconscious and later taken into POC custody — clearly the same two men from the footage.
That confirms the two attacks are the work of the same crew. Before the authorities arrived, the surviving intruder mentioned Ven Yasha but gave little else.
The third man is still unaccounted for. A shooter stayed outside throughout and did not come in. Whether that’s the red-haired man with The Device is unestablished — but the attack opened the same way as the hostel job, with power and security knocked out first.
Pallod Norrim later said the POC had arrested Darrian Jak for Vlen’s murder and confirmed that Jak is short and red-haired. That matches the third man’s broad description, but it is not an independent identification.
Open questions

Who the two Dancado attackers were, and who sent them
Whether all three went into Vlen’s room, and how many came out
Whether the red-haired man deliberately kept off camera — see The Device
Whether the shooter who stayed outside at Dancado is the third man
Whether Darrian Jak is the red-haired third man or a convenient suspect

Notes

travellers'-aid-society.title: Travellers' Aid Society
travellers'-aid-society.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
TAS. Vlen Backett was staying at their Regina Down TAS Hostel in Credo City when he was killed, and their security camera caught the Three Men at Vlen’s Room — so TAS holds the footage.
Expanded from “TAS” on the board; the board itself only ever writes the initials.
Notes

tusal.title: Tusal
tusal.content:
traveller sota item
Secrets of the Ancients
An illegal narcotic, usually sold as tablets, though some prefer it in its less processed, undried form as a wad to be chewed. Derived from a seaweed.
Origin unknown, but believed to have been imported from the Vargr extents about a century ago. Now grown on various worlds along the Corridor sector.
Effects

A dose produces mild euphoria and intoxication
A very strong dose dulls pain receptors and causes unconsciousness
Users stay functional on a low dose, so many addicts chew six or seven tablets a day to hold a constant drugged haze

Who uses it
Especially associated with menial jobs and the unemployed — an otherwise dull life of drudgery made pleasant. Long-term addiction brings respiratory and digestive problems and a high incidence of stomach cancer.
Bearing on the murder
Vlen Backett had 200 ng/mL in his blood when he died — per the coroner, enough that he would barely have been able to stand, let alone fight back. That is squarely the “very strong dose” band: pain receptors dulled, heading for unconsciousness.
Two things that don’t fit a recreational user:

The drug’s user base is menial labourers and the unemployed holding a low functional dose. Vlen was neither, and his dose was nowhere near low.
A man that sedated doesn’t wander into a very strong dose by accident and then happen to be shot through the heart at close range with no defensive wounds.

It reads as a dose given to him to make the killing easy — inference, not established. See Vlen Backett’s Murder.
Darrian Jak sold a lot of Tusal in Credo City the night Vlen died — the party’s best lead on where this batch came from.
Loose thread
Tusal is believed to have come out of the Vargr extents. Vlen was a man that Vargr crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult. Probably nothing — the drug’s been in Imperial space a century and is grown locally — but it’s noted.
Notes

tyrus-cassius.title: Tyrus Cassius
tyrus-cassius.content:
traveller sota character
Secrets of the Ancients
Admiral Tyrus Cassius — player character. Owns the Pinnace Implacable, carried by the Event Horizon.
Originally named Cmdr Valarian; renamed to Cassius. Anything recorded elsewhere under the old name refers to him.
Naval officer Kostas Backett served under. Led a mutiny that failed; Kostas backed it and was punished for it, Cassius apparently was not — he’s since retired as an Admiral. Kostas talked his way aboard the Event Horizon to find him and demand a job.
Aylin Boro, a retired admiral and one of Kostas’ contacts, hates him.
Appearance

Older man, greying dark hair, waxed moustache. Dark naval dress uniform — heavy gold braid at the cuffs, epaulettes, aiguillette, medal ribbons and orders at the breast — with a long greatcoat worn over the shoulders and his cap under one arm. Dressed for ceremony, not for work.
Notes

After the attack at Dancado, Cassius began tying up the unconscious intruder while the rest of the crew tried to restore the autodoc and retrieve Iaros Ujinka.
Cassius reported the Dancado attack to Chief Inspector Pallod Norrim.
He used his network to build influence on Regina beyond Pallod and learned about the Alahir, its captain’s repeated meetings with Pallod, and offworlders reportedly operating in POC uniforms.
His network also reported that an Imperial police force had taken over a murder inquiry as state security, with the dead man rumoured to have been a Zhodani spy. The claims remain unverified.
196-1105: went back into Credo with Ozy to check Winter Shipping’s office — Exceedingly Discreet gone, nothing found. Offered his savings to fund the trip. Vetted the passengers on Streetwise. Ran the jump to Forboldn (astrogation Effect +1, jump roll +6). Training in jump — eight weeks needed

uakye.title: Uakye
uakye.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
Tidally locked, so all settlements sit in the habitable ‘twilight zone’.
Closely associated with Efate, but Countess Parasii strongly affirms her planet’s independence from “the technocracy one system over”.
Notes

Given by the GM on 196-1105 as Ozy’s homeworld — “right next door to Alell”

ujinka's-research.title: Ujinka's Research
ujinka's-research.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Iaros Ujinka was investigating links between G-Band Transmissions and sites of Ancient technology. That’s what took her to Beck’s World, and it is what she and Vlen Backett were going to discuss.
Vlen’s involvement
Vlen was going to provide funding and a ship to support the research. That is the “topics of mutual interest” from his letter — and it means a drifter with no visible income was in a position to bankroll a university research programme and put a hull under it.
He was murdered before the meeting happened.
The proposal to the party
Before her death, Ujinka asked whether the party could use the Event Horizon to support the research instead. No final answer given yet.
The Event Horizon is a Lab Ship. She is, functionally, exactly the vessel this research needs — and Graxius StClair, who owns her, is Ujinka’s former student.
Worth knowing: Kaldi Research runs lab ships for hire throughout the Marches. Ujinka could have chartered a professional research vessel. She asked a dead man’s nephew’s crew instead.
Why this matters
Vlen agreed to fund and crew an expedition to Ancient sites, and was shot before he could. Ujinka was then shot dead in her own house, minutes after explaining the research to a second set of potential backers.
Two people, one project, both murdered inside four days. Someone is killing to stop this research — and they knew where and when to find her.
Who would care
Ancients sites cluster in the Spinward Marches, and their technology runs beyond TL25. A reliable method of finding those sites — which is what G-Band Transmissions would be — is worth killing for. Two movements on record already stake their theology on Ancients inheritance:

Church of the Chosen Ones — Vargr are the Ancients’ rightful heirs
Brotherhood of Humaniti — the Ancients broke humanity, and opposing institutions must be destroyed

Nobody has been placed at either murder.
What survives her

The party, who heard it from her directly
Data recovered by Ozy from her house at Dancado — three research notes, transcribed below
Beck’s World, where the fieldwork was, and where Graxius StClair’s ex-wife still is
The University of Regina, her department
The Event Horizon, still the right ship for it, and the decision now nobody’s to accept

The research notes — recovered 196-1105
Three notes Ozy pulled off Ujinka’s computer at Dancado, shared by the GM aboard the Event Horizon on 196-1105. Text as given.
Research Note 1

Subject: Anomalous Attenuation of G-Band Radio Frequencies in Proximity to Purported Precursor Sites.
…While conventional Imperial archaeology treats the Boughene and Regina precursor ruins as chemically inert, localized sensor logs paint a radically different picture. During the 1102 survey, standard subspace telemetry in the G-band suffered a sharp, recursive drop-off. This is not natural solar radiation or iron-ore interference. It mimics a low-frequency, multi-phasic dampening field — a passive ‘footprint’ left by active Monadium structures buried deep beneath the mantle. If my calculations are correct, we can map hidden sites not by looking for ruins, but by looking for the communication ‘dead zones’ they cast across a system.

A later added note states:

Juni and her team will be investigating these G-band signals further at the Beck’s World ancients site. I wonder what secrets she will uncover.

Research Note 2


Log Entry 884-A: Orbiting Gas Giant (Boughene IV). High metal-rich asteroid density.
Telemetry: Ship sensor packet degradation detected at 4.2 GHz (G-band). Automated navigation computers experienced a 0.03-second clock-drift.
Ujinka’s Scribbled Margin Note: “The trader wasn’t lying. The statue he pulled from the asteroid belt is a fragment of a larger anchor array. The signal dampening here perfectly matches the footprint I isolated in the Regina sub-sector. Could something else be hidden away in this system? Vlen Backett thinks the system is worth studying, he has asked to borrow the statue apparently for analysis by one of his contacts.”


Research Note 3

Notes from the Deneb Archeological Conference: The Vilani records from thousands of years ago are fundamentally flawed. They logged the site at Kan as just another ‘precursor society’. They lacked the conceptual leap. They found shimmering glass harder than diamond and containers made of unblemished, un-corroded cobalt, yet they classified it as dead rubbish. It isn’t a collection of disparate alien species. It is a single, unified entity that wielded localised physics like paintbrushes. They didn’t just build structures; they engineered the very matter to resist time.

What the notes establish

The method: Ancient sites cast g-band “dead zones” across a system. Find the dead zone, find the site — no ruins needed. Ujinka attributes the dampening to buried “Monadium structures” (her term; not otherwise explained)
Two confirmed footprints: the Regina sub-sector (the 1102 survey) and Boughene, at the asteroid belt around Boughene IV. Boughene’s official description says there is nothing there of interest
The statue is from Boughene. A trader pulled it from the belt; Ujinka judged it a fragment of a larger anchor array; Vlen borrowed it. It is now the statuette on the Event Horizon. The ship’s scans call it a work of art, not a device, and of Ancients origin
Vlen’s disks corroborate all of this and add a note from Vlen reminding himself to acquire the Professor’s g-band sensor system and use it to scan the Boughene system. Vlen had a target, not just an interest
Juni — Graxius StClair’s ex-wife — has taken the g-band work to the Ancients site on Beck’s World and is there now
Note 3 is a thesis about The Ancients rather than about the signals: one unified entity, not many species, that “wielded localised physics like paintbrushes” and built matter to resist time. The Vilani saw the site at Kan and misfiled it as rubbish

Notes

The crew have not yet decided whether to commit the Event Horizon to continuing the research.
196-1105: the ship left Regina for Alell carrying the notes, the statue and Vlen’s disks. No formal answer given, but the material is aboard

university-of-regina.title: University of Regina
university-of-regina.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
Commonly used to refer to any of several prestigious academic institutions on Regina. Collectively, the University of Regina is the largest and most successful higher-level education and research facility in the Spinward Marches.
Iaros Ujinka was a professor in its Department of History — until she was murdered. Her department, her colleagues and her papers are all still there, and are the obvious next place to look for whatever she knew about Ujinka’s Research.
Notes

vargr.title: Vargr
vargr.content:
traveller sota species
Secrets of the Ancients
A species found outside the Imperium, in territory referred to as the Vargr extents. Tusal is believed to have been imported from there roughly a century ago.
Uplifted from Terran canines by The Ancients — which makes them one of the few living things with a direct claim on the Ancients’ legacy, and the Church of the Chosen Ones builds a whole theology on exactly that.
Vargr in the file so far

40th Squadron — organised Vargr power bloc in Gvurrdon, previously bankrolled by the Zhodani
Church of the Chosen Ones — fringe sect holding Vargr to be the Ancients’ rightful heirs
Menorb — agricultural world feeding the Vargr market, raided for it
Rynkatropa — a TL1 sophont species the Vargr enslaved
Tusal — the narcotic that killed Vlen Backett came out of the Vargr extents
Vargr once crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult Vlen himself

On at least one occasion, Vargr travelled hundreds of parsecs to consult Vlen Backett — the single strangest thing in his address book, and the clearest sign his interests reach well beyond Imperial space.
Notes

ven-yasha.title: Ven Yasha
ven-yasha.content:
traveller sota npc rival
Secrets of the Ancients
Rival. A mysterious crime lord, wanted by numerous worlds around Regina. Location unknown.
No-one has ever seen them, so the wanted bulletins are extremely vague. Gender, species, whether “Ven Yasha” is even one person — all unknown.
Connection to Kostas
Kostas Backett has had plenty of issues throughout his career. Just the once, he put out feelers on who was behind one of them, and only one name came back.
Whispers from the shadows, a piece of paper found under a door, hushed exchanges with a contact — whatever went wrong and whenever he went looking for who was behind it, it was just a name and nothing more.
Connection to Vlen
His name kept cropping up in connection with Vlen Backett as well. Iaros Ujinka doesn’t know him personally, only by reputation — and says he is very unpleasant.
So the same name attaches to both Kostas’ career troubles and his murdered uncle’s affairs. That is either the single most important fact in the investigation or a coincidence of a very common bogeyman.
The surviving intruder from the attack at Dancado mentioned Ven Yasha during the crew’s brief questioning before the POC arrived. He gave little else, so the nature of the connection remains unknown.
Odoy’s account — 195-1105
Detective Odoy is investigating Ven Yasha, and told the crew that Yasha killed Vlen Backett and that Vlen was working as a courier for Yasha. He also says the Imperial force that arrived aboard the Alahir is on Regina hunting Yasha, with the Zhodani-spy story serving as cover for their takeover of the inquiry.
None of this is independently verified — it is Odoy’s word, and his own agency and motives are unknown. But it is now the second independent source naming Yasha: the surviving Dancado attacker did so too, before the Imperials removed him from POC custody.
If Odoy is right, the courier theory would explain Vlen’s constant travel and his improbable address book.
Open questions

Who is Ven Yasha?
If Vlen was his courier, what was Vlen carrying — and does it connect to Ujinka’s Research?
Why an Imperial force would cross to Regina to hunt him
How many of Kostas’ career problems are actually theirs? Only one was ever traced.
What the connection to Vlen actually is — creditor, rival, employer, killer?
Whether “he” is right: Ujinka uses it, but nobody has ever seen the man

From inside Winter Shipping â€” 196-1105
Exceedingly Discreet, the Llellewyoly who keeps Winter Shipping’s real records, spoke about Yasha freely on some points and refused others outright. All unverified:

Yasha hired the whole Winter Shipping operation, Harlen included. The company is his
Yasha ordered Iaros Ujinka’s death. Exceedingly Discreet does not understand why, and says so â€” greater understanding of Ancient technology would only raise the value of Ancient artefacts. It does not question his requests
Vlen Backett was a messenger for Yasha â€” “he must have brought bad news, hence his demise”. This is a second, independent version of Detective Odoy’s courier claim
On what Yasha wants from Ancient technology: nobody understands the secrets of the Ancients, but the potential runs to immortality, taking systems, taking the Imperium, destroying armies. Exceedingly Discreet knows of no specific plan
It will not discuss Yasha himself â€” information about Harlen, the hired thugs and Imperial Intelligence is on offer; Yasha is “very much off the cards”, for its own survival. Going against him is “a very bad idea”

Three sources now attach Yasha to the case â€” the Dancado prisoner, Detective Odoy, and now his own organisation.
Notes

vlen-backett's-murder.title: Vlen Backett's Murder
vlen-backett's-murder.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
Vlen Backett was murdered in Credo City. From the coroner’s report:

Cause of death: low-velocity gunshot wound to the heart, delivered at close range
Defensive wounds: none
Blood test: 200 ng/mL of the narcotic Tusal — at that level he would barely have been able to stand, let alone fight back. That’s in the “very strong dose” band: pain receptors dulled, heading toward unconsciousness
Augmentations: none

Drugged first, then shot through the heart from close range, with no attempt to defend himself. That reads as an execution rather than a fight or a robbery gone wrong — inference, not stated in the report.
Low-velocity and close range also suggests a quiet weapon and someone who got near enough to use it — worth knowing whether Vlen let them get that close.
What the investigation has since established

Vlen arrived on Regina from Rhylanor three days before he died
He was staying at the Regina Down TAS Hostel, and their camera caught the Three Men at Vlen’s Room — two faces, and a third who kept off camera but had red hair
He was on Regina to meet Iaros Ujinka, a historian he already knew — a meeting arranged before he arrived, and one he never made
Iaros Ujinka has since been murdered too, at Dancado, minutes after explaining the same research to the party — and the party killed one of the two intruders and captured the other, both men from the hostel footage, tying the attacks to one crew
The meeting was to agree funding and a ship for Ujinka’s Research into Ancient technology sites. The first credible motive: he was about to put money and a hull behind an Ancients expedition
Ven Yasha’s name kept cropping up in connection with Vlen
The third carried The Device, which seems to have caused electrical interference
Darrian Jak, a local dealer, sold a lot of Tusal the night Vlen died. Pallod Norrim now claims the short, red-haired Jak killed Vlen, but the crew have not independently verified that conclusion
His Smashed Comms yielded one last number before becoming unusable: Winter Shipping
Admiral Cassius’s network reports that an Imperial police force has taken over a murder inquiry as a state-security matter, with the victim rumoured to be a Zhodani spy. Whether that inquiry and victim are Vlen’s is unconfirmed

Running state in Investigation Status.
Open questions

Who the three men are, and who sent them
Whether the Tusal was self-administered or given to him
Whether this is what the Regina Public Order Commission means by Irregularities in Vlen Backett’s Affairs, or something separate
What he was doing on Rhylanor, and whether he was followed from there
Whether Pallod’s case against Darrian Jak is genuine, mistaken or a cover story
Why Vlen’s last recovered call was to Winter Shipping

Notes

vlen-backett's-true-age.title: Vlen Backett's True Age
vlen-backett's-true-age.content:
traveller sota clue
Secrets of the Ancients
The coroner’s report on Vlen Backett states:

Physiological age: 52
Historical records indicate true age at least 180
No sign of anagathics in his blood system
No augmentations

He was at least 180 years old, had the body of a 52-year-old, and there is no chemical explanation for it.
Every relative who knew him as “every child’s favourite uncle” knew a man who had been doing that for generations. Kostas Backett is 38.
Open questions

How
Whether he knew what he was
Whether it connects to his archaeology, his unnamed contacts among scientists and high nobility, or the Vargr who crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult him
Whether whoever killed him knew

Notes

Kostas researched Vlen’s age again before the meeting with Odoy but found nothing new.

vlen-backett.title: Vlen Backett
vlen-backett.content:
traveller sota npc ally
Secrets of the Ancients
Ally. Murdered. “Uncle Vlen” — Kostas Backett’s extended family. Homeworld Alell.
Human. Physiologically 52 at death; historical records put his true age at at least 180, with no anagathics in his blood — see Vlen Backett’s True Age. Killed by a close-range gunshot to the heart while drugged senseless — see Vlen Backett’s Murder.
Took Kostas under his wing plenty of times throughout his troubled career — without Vlen’s “loans” he may never have made it. The scare quotes are the character sheet’s own; on what terms is unstated.
Character
Only at home when travelling. He’d visit Alell for a few weeks or a month or two, delighting friends and family with tales of distant planets and exotic cultures, then the wanderlust would take him off again. A charming old rogue — the more staid relatives disapproved of his questionable, unreliable ways, but he was every child’s favourite uncle.
What he actually does
No-one was ever sure, or whether he was just a drifter amid the stars.

Worked tramp traders, signed on as a deckhand on freighters
Dabbled in archaeology and journalism
Never liked to talk about it, but had quite a collection of firearms and could handle himself in a fight

His strange friends
Mostly other space voyagers — but he received irregular communications from scientists, naval officers, corporate oligarchs, even high nobility. On at least one occasion, Vargr from outside the Imperium travelled hundreds of parsecs to consult with him.
That detail reads differently now: the Vargr were uplifted by The Ancients, Vlen was funding a hunt for Ancients sites, and he was killed with a narcotic that came out of the Vargr extents.
None of these contacts are named. The archaeology plus the reach of that address book is a lot of smoke for a man with no visible job — worth pulling on.
What he was doing on Regina
He came to meet Iaros Ujinka and agree terms on Ujinka’s Research — he was going to provide the funding and a ship for an expedition to sites of Ancient technology. He was killed three days after arriving, before the meeting happened.
Ven Yasha’s name kept cropping up in connection with him.
The last recoverable call from his smashed comms was to Winter Shipping, a logistics and cargo-buying company operating in Credo City and Star Town.
Death
Murdered in Credo City on Regina, late of Regina/Alell. The coroner’s report gives the details (Vlen Backett’s Murder, Vlen Backett’s True Age); the Commission’s letter, below, never mentions that he was killed at all. Notified to Kostas Backett by Pallod Norrim of the Regina Public Order Commission — Handout 2, “Message from Regina”, sealed 190 Standard, 1105 Third Imperium.

Before his death, Vlen left instructions on file with the Public Order Commission naming Kostas as next of kin — to resolve his outstanding affairs on Regina, take possession of his belongings, and transport his remains back to Alell.
A sum of money is deposited with the First Ducal Bank to cover expenses.
His body is in a cryogenic facility in Credo City, to be transferred to Kostas as soon as possible. A TL14+ autodoc can reanimate a corpse kept in a low berth or cryoberth for up to 1D days after death — Vlen died on or before 190-1105 and it is now 193. Probably outside the window, and no one has raised it, but the body is in cryo and Kostas is the legal next of kin who takes possession of it.
Kostas is required, in the name of the Duke and under the Public Order Act of 527 (Amended), to travel to Regina with all due haste — or reply so alternate arrangements can be made.
“Given certain irregularities with Vlen Backett’s affairs, it is vitally important that you contact the Public Order Commission upon arrival.” See Irregularities in Vlen Backett’s Affairs.

Two oddities in the letter itself: it’s addressed to the “chattels and corpus of Vlen Backett (deceased)” rather than to Kostas by name, and the Chief Inspector signs off as Pallod Norum having opened as Pallod Norrim.
Pallod now claims that short, red-haired Darrian Jak murdered Vlen and considers the case closed. The crew have not independently verified that conclusion and distrust Pallod’s dismissal of the connected events at Dancado.
The courier theory
On 195-1105 Detective Odoy told the crew that Vlen was a courier for Ven Yasha, and that Yasha killed him — not Jak. Odoy also says the rumour of a murdered Zhodani spy refers to Vlen, that Vlen was not a spy, and that the story is a cover for the Imperial takeover of the inquiry.
All unverified. It would, though, account for a man with no visible job, constant travel, and an address book running from scientists to high nobility — and it sits alongside his last recovered call going to Winter Shipping, where Odoy places the fixer Harlen.
Unresolved: whether courier work and the funding of Ujinka’s Research are the same thread or two separate lives.
Corroboration from inside Winter Shipping â€” 196-1105
Exceedingly Discreet independently described Vlen as a messenger for Ven Yasha â€” “he must have brought bad news, hence his demise”. That is a second source for the courier theory above, and the first to give a motive for the killing, however offhand.
It also says Harlen holds Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals â€” property of Vlen’s that never reached the POC-held estate.
Notes

vlen's-statuette-and-data-crystals.title: Vlen's Statuette and Data Crystals
vlen's-statuette-and-data-crystals.content:
traveller sota item
Secrets of the Ancients
Recovered on 196-1105. A statuette and a set of data disks, taken off Harlen’s desk aboard the hidden base by Ozy in the last thirty seconds before it self-destructed. Harlen was sitting right there with his eyes closed and was not interfered with.
Originally volunteered by Exceedingly Discreet in the small hours of 196-1105, unprompted — “it would be amiss if I didn’t mention that, seeing as you are his nephew” — as possessions of Vlen Backett’s that Harlen was holding.
Are they Vlen’s?
Presumed so, on strong circumstantial grounds, but never confirmed in the fiction. What lines up:

Exceedingly Discreet named a statuette and data crystals in Harlen’s hands, and a statuette and data disks are exactly what was on his desk
They were not part of the estate the POC are holding
Nobody at the table heard Harlen or anyone else say whose they were

The wording also drifted — “crystals” from Exceedingly Discreet, “disks” as described on the desk. Probably the same objects.
The statuette
Ozy recognised it as the same sort of thing that was in Professor Ujinka’s house — his Recon roll was poor and he has no relevant expertise, so this is a layman’s resemblance and no more. If it holds, it makes this the first physical object tying Vlen, Ujinka’s Research and Ven Yasha’s organisation together, and very likely an Ancient artefact.
Vlen was funding Ujinka’s work. Ven Yasha had Ujinka killed for reasons his own records-keeper could not explain. This object sat on the desk of the man who ran Yasha’s company.
Examined — 196-1105
Aboard the Event Horizon, scanned with the ship’s sensors and read against Ujinka’s research notes:
The statuette is a winged pillar of an ivory-like substance. The scans say a work of art, not a technological device, and all evidence points to it being of Ancients origin. It is the statue from Ujinka’s Research Note 2 — pulled by a trader from the asteroid belt around Boughene IV in the Boughene system, which Ujinka judged to be a fragment of a larger anchor array. Her margin note records that Vlen asked to borrow it “for analysis by one of his contacts”. He evidently got it; how it ended up on Harlen’s desk is not explained.
The disks corroborate the match, cover the Boughene asteroid belt and the g-band fluctuations there, and include a note from Vlen reminding himself to acquire the Professor’s g-band sensor system and use it to scan the Boughene system. Only that much of their contents has been described so far.
The data disks
Partly read — see above. The rest not yet described.
Open questions

What the statuette actually is, and whether it is Ancient — Ancient art, an anchor-array fragment from Boughene
What is on the disks — and whether it overlaps with the material Ozy already recovered from Ujinka
Why they were on Harlen’s desk rather than with Ven Yasha
Who Vlen’s “contact” for the analysis was, and whether that contact was Ven Yasha
Whether reading the disks is safe, given what happened to everyone else who knew what Ujinka was working on

Notes

whanga.title: Whanga
whanga.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
World on the Event Horizon’s route from Regina to Alell: Forboldn → Whanga → Alell, the second of three jumps. Has a gas giant for skimming fuel. The table found the name funny.
Nothing else known yet.
Notes

whisperhawk.title: Whisperhawk
whisperhawk.content:
traveller sota species
Secrets of the Ancients
An animal. One of the most common sights in the Alell jungle — beautiful avians with prodigious wingspans.
Their wings are both locomotion and feeding organs: whisperhawks feed by digesting the insects caught on the sticky undersides. A flock gliding across the canopy at twilight catches hundreds of thousands of insects; the buzzing of the trapped insects and the susurrus of the wind gives the whisperhawk its name.
They are notoriously stupid and have been known to attack humans and vehicles, as well as flagposts, fences, houses and small trees. If threatened, a whisperhawk attacks by wrapping its wings around a larger foe and trying to smother it.
Notes

winter-shipping-station.title: Winter Shipping Station
winter-shipping-station.content:
traveller sota location
Secrets of the Ancients
Destroyed on 196-1105. Harlen triggered its self-destruct while the crew were aboard; the crew escaped by capsule and watched it go.
Called “the station we have in orbit” and “the base” by Exceedingly Discreet, which flew the crew up to it. It was never a station. It was three shipping containers bolted together, hidden inside a container yard at a semi-stable Lagrangian point between Regina and Assiniboia — the same sort of point Assiniboia is noted for. Anything parked there stays put for years.
The approach ran through a constellation of cargo containers, thousands of them, docked into long lines and cubes with some drifting free and untethered, scattered with nav buoys and warning beacons. The launch weaved into the heart of the yard, dipped beneath a trio of old containers, and a concealed hatch opened to dock it inside. Nothing about it was visible or registered as a structure.
This was the destination of the launch runs that took hours longer than a surface-to-Highport trip should — the anomaly Ozy found in the hacked flight manifests.
What was inside

No lights, anywhere. The staff knew their way around in the dark
Doors barely airtight — on a structure in vacuum — and everything cobbled together from salvage
A dock bay of roughly 20 by 50 feet holding the launch and a few sealed crates
An upper level reached by an airlock and ladder, with cover scattered through it, an office, and what looked like a gun emplacement
Harlen’s office, with a statuette and data disks on the desk — see Vlen’s Statuette and Data Crystals
A capsule deck with several escape capsules, each big enough for five. Two were locked and jammed when the smugglers reached them
A crew of smugglers — the GM’s word for them — the number never established. At least seven died

The destruct
Harlen saw Kostas, recognised him, looked at Cassius’ uniform, said “This is suboptimal” and closed his eyes. Every screen in the base went black, an alarm sounded, and a synthesised voice announced destruct sequence activated, detonation imminent, all hands to re-entry capsules, with floor arrows lighting a route to the capsule airlock.
Thirty seconds. No console, no keypad, no spoken command — see Harlen.
About twenty seconds after the capsule launched the base imploded, scrunched up and then blew outward. The capsule rode the edge of the wave down to Regina and landed in wild land outside the Twin Cities, at what looked like a designated recovery point with grav bikes waiting.
What went with it

Whatever Winter Shipping was actually moving through the overlong runs — never established
Any records held on the base rather than in Exceedingly Discreet’s head in Credo
Most of its staff
Possibly Harlen himself, who was last seen at his desk as the count ran down

Notes

winter-shipping.title: Winter Shipping
winter-shipping.content:
traveller sota faction
Secrets of the Ancients
A logistics and cargo-buying company operating in both Credo City and Star Town, the thin strip between Credo and Atora.
The last number called from Vlen Backett’s smashed comms belongs to Winter Shipping. Ozy recovered the number immediately before the damaged device became unusable.
Its advertising targets ship crews struggling with mortgage payments, salaries or repair bills. It offers to buy their cargo with the promise: “Prompt service. No questions asked.”

The premises — reconnoitred 195-1105
Two buildings, one either side of the fence between Credo City and Star Town. The crew approached from the Credo side.

The Credo-side building is closed, with a notice directing callers to the Star Town offices
A huge brute of a man was seen entering the Credo side and emerging on the Star Town side — a crossing that is not supposed to be possible. The crew infer an internal passage through the fence; unconfirmed
The Star Town office interior is very fancy, far smarter than its surroundings. Marid works reception
